additional_considerations.rationale: An uncommon coxsackievirus illness with acute severe paroxysmal chest or abdominal pain worse with cough or breathing; usually resolves within 3 days to 1 week.
Another cause of acute cough; alcoholic, elderly and neurologically impaired patients are at risk.
Extremely rare in a young patient with no risk factors.
Signs and symptoms of heart failure would be present.
His sexual history warrants HIV screening, but there is no sign of immunosuppression (e.g. thrush) and PJP cough is usually nonproductive with dyspnea.

source_issues: The note exam vital signs line (e002) gives only 'Low-grade fever' without values; the doorway vitals give 99.9°F (37.7°C) and normal BP, RR and HR.

Exam e005 'Increased tactile fremitus and decreased breath sounds on the right side' does not say explicitly that the fremitus is right-sided; the sp_notes simulate both findings on the right chest, so both were recorded as right-sided.
p008 'I can't take a deep breath' sits uneasily with the denial of shortness of breath in p017; both recorded literally.
p014 and p017 use the stock answer 'No, I do not.' for a recent-exposure question and a list of symptoms; the denials are clear.
The raw examinee task list repeats 'Write the patient note after leaving the room.' (task 5).
annotator_notes: The preceding URI (p002) is split into runny nose, fever and sore throat, each 'resolved' with the timing two weeks ago, lasting a week.
The current slight fever (p003) is 'current' because it is reported as part of the present illness, although he did not measure it.
p006/p009 (pain triggered and worsened by cough and deep breathing) are merged into f009; p006 'sharp' and p008 'like a knife' are merged into f011.

The two sp_notes chest maneuvers are recorded as sp_notes exam findings (x008, x009) describing what the SP does and the sign it simulates; the coughing directions are kept as acting notes only, as in the worked example.
'Other etiologies' in the additional diagnoses is split into aspiration, pulmonary embolism, pulmonary edema and HIV/PJP.
